key_insight: Compressing a streaming geometry transformer's KV memory is not just a precision trade-off: different cache locations have different geometric sensitivity, and retrieval errors can disrupt downstream geometry predictions.
problem_solved: Historical key-value caches preserve cross-view geometric information but grow during long-sequence inference. Low-bit compression must reduce this memory burden without undermining geometric consistency.
method: Systematically characterize KV quantization across precision choices and cache locations.
Identify two linked challenges: Nonuniform Geometric Sensitivity and Cache-Geometry Mismatch.
Target geometry-aligned low-bit KV caching; the provided abstract is truncated and does not specify the full implementation.
impact: This work highlights why KV compression for visual geometry should account for geometric sensitivity rather than memory savings alone. It could help practitioners design more memory-efficient long-sequence inference, though the excerpt provides no quantitative results.
visual_elements: Streaming frames feeding a growing KV cache, contrasted with a compact low-bit cache.
Heatmap showing quantization sensitivity across cache locations and precision levels.
Error-propagation diagram: perturbed retrieval → changed geometry-head inputs → downstream geometry errors.
Two warning icons labeling Nonuniform Geometric Sensitivity and Cache-Geometry Mismatch.
paper_title: QuantStream3D: Geometry-Aligned Low-Bit KV Cache Quantization for Streaming Visual Geometry Transformers
paper_authors: Zunhai Su, Keyu Fan, Ruishan Guo, Zhongzhu Zhou, Jingzehua Xu
